messages:
Aisha: heads-up — ran a quick per-layer int4 sensitivity sweep on prod-v2 (dev cluster) this morning, excluding embeddings + lm_head. putting results here for visibility
Ben: nice, what did you test exactly?
Aisha: baseline = fp16 all-layers. experiments: (1) int4 everywhere (2) int4 w/ embeddings+lm_head kept fp16 (3) int4 w/ first 2 transformer layers kept fp16 (4) mixed int4/int8 by kernel-selector heuristics. each run used the same 2M-sample prompt set, KV warm/cold split 80/20, batch target 32, async batching on
Carlos: any perf numbers?
Aisha: perf highlights: int4-all -> +1.95x tokens/sec vs fp16 but regen rate up ~3.1% on our eval prompts. int4+embed/lm_fp16 -> +1.82x tokens/sec, regen +0.9%. int4+first2_fp16 -> +1.76x tokens/sec, regen +0.7%. mixed int4/int8 by selector -> +1.83x tokens/sec, regen +0.5%
Maya: so excluding embeddings+lm_head recovers most quality at small cost to perf — seems promising
Ben: calibration effects? did you run per-layer calibration or global?
Aisha: ran both. per-layer calibration reduced regen by ~0.3% vs global, but added ~6% extra calibration time on the offline pipeline. interestingly, per-layer calibrations for FFN-heavy layers pushed some kernels into a slow fp-fallback path on our A100-like nodes — profiler showed kernel_launch_count spiking and ~12% more device-side idle while host waited for kernel selection
Carlos: can you paste profiler snippet?
Aisha: sure:
```
# from /tmp/rdw-perf/scan-1842/prof.txt
Layer 12 (FFN): kernel=int4_ffn_gemm v2 -> exec_time=2.3ms, l2_misses=1.9e6
Layer 13 (FFN): kernel=fp-fallback_gemm -> exec_time=5.7ms, l2_misses=2.4e6
KV cache warm hit rate: 82% (cold paths had 2.1x latency)
Batching: avg batch=27 vs target 32 (due to tail latency cap)
Kernel selection time (host): 0.12ms/op avg, but spiked to 1.8ms for layers with per-layer calib metadata
```
Maya: so calibration metadata is pushing selector to re-evaluate kernel per-request? that explains host-side stalls
Aisha: yeah selector currently does a small hash lookup+policy apply per-request per-layer when per-layer calib flags exist — cheap usually but with many small requests it adds up. also observed more kernel churn which increases kernel launch overhead
Ben: what about KV cache interaction? any differences with cold/warm split?
Aisha: cold paths amplify the perf delta. int4-all cold -> 2.3x slower than warm int4 (due to repeated recompute and worse kernel warmup). excluding embeddings + lm_head reduced cold penalty by ~18% because those layers are hot in early tokens and being fp16 avoids expensive fallbacks
Carlos: any qualitative failures (hallucinations) concentrated in specific layers?
Aisha: yes — a small subset of middle transformer layers (roughly layers 9-14) are highly sensitive; partial float for those layers reduced token-level divergence a lot. embeddings/lm_head exclusion fixed most tokenization/unknown-token regressions
Maya: actionable suggestions?
Aisha: propose a heuristic: 1) default int4 for attention & most FFNs, 2) keep embeddings and lm_head fp16, 3) mark layers 9-14 as 'sensitive' -> prefer int8 rather than fp16 to keep perf up, 4) add a per-request fastpath in kernel-selector to skip per-layer policy checks when request_size > threshold or kv_warm==true
Ben: sounds good. any numbers for the heuristic?
Aisha: simulated canary: heuristic -> +1.78x tokens/sec vs fp16, regen +0.4% vs baseline, cold penalty down 12% vs int4-all. kernel-selector optimized fastpath cut host-side kernel decision time from 0.12ms -> 0.03ms
Carlos: can we implement fastpath without breaking rollout logic?
Maya: yes if we make it an override policy with explicit flags: selector.fastpath_enabled + request_hints. we'll keep canary gate on rollout manager
DeployBot: deploy plan template created: https://ci.redwood.local/pipelines/rdw-canary/1842 (needs owner +1)
Ben: next steps: Aisha to PR selector fastpath + unit tests, Maya to add per-layer sensitivity table to model onboarding, Carlos to create canary job with kv cold/warm toggle. target: small canary on dedicated for 48h
Aisha: I'll open the PR this afternoon and attach the perf traces.
Maya: I'll update model-card and add a note for the ops runbook about monitoring regen-rate + kv-hit-rate during canary
Carlos: will schedule canary after PR lands. thanks all :thumbsup:
Aisha: thanks — piling these traces into the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/1842-int4-scan/
